thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: [SEV-2] multi-region failover paused. traffic-shift ap-southeast-1 -> eu-central-1 stalled at ~61% after 6m; ingestion and streaming timeouts increasing. Paging @sam_oncall and @rachel_network

maya_ops: Ack. oncall here, pulling dashboards. Which endpoints are noisy?

sam_oncall: I'm on it. p95 & 5xx up for streaming and file-ingest paths originating from AP edge. Runbook: https://rwd.internal/runbooks/traffic-shift#multi-region. First glance: control-plane shows desired eu-central-1=100, actual=61.

rachel_network: Route snapshots: two AP POPs (ap-pop-5, ap-pop-12) still advertising AP origin prefixes. Withdrawal RPCs to those POPs show no ack. I also see routecache entries pinned to the old origin in fastpath for those POPs.

priya_prod: Probing edge node ap-pop-12 health: 

```
$ curl -fsS http://edge-ap-pop-12.internal/health || true
{"status":"degraded","checks":{"upstream-lb":false,"routecache_pinned":true}}
```

priya_prod: LB upstream returning intermittent 502, and routecache shows stale entries.

rachel_network: Checked cloud provider console: they reported a control-plane throttling window impacting route withdrawal calls in ap-southeast-1 (ticket CP-202340). Some withdraws are queued/dropped.

maya_ops: Ok. Options: A) wait for provider fix (may be minutes), B) manual reweight to eu-central (risk cache churn), C) force-pop withdraw at edge-orch (aggressive, will cause client reconnects). Input?

jules_support: Support seeing several mid-tier customers with retries on ingest. Enterprise customers not fully degraded yet but retry storm increasing costs. We're ready to push short status updates.

sam_oncall: I prefer a measured manual reweight first (+25% to eu-central) with canary and preserve_cache to limit CPU and cache-miss impact. Executing admin reweight now.

```
# canary reweight
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/v1/traffic/reweight" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"from_region":"ap-southeast-1","to_region":"eu-central-1","delta_percent":25,"canary":true,"preserve_cache":true}'
```

incident-bot: Action recorded: manual_reweight by sam_oncall at 3721120050

maya_ops: Reweight applied. watching metrics...

(20s pass)

sam_oncall: Partial recovery: eu-central weight -> 86%, aggregate 5xx dropped to ~5% but ap-pop-5 and ap-pop-12 still serve ~24% of traffic and keep returning 502/timeout. Provider still shows pending withdraws for those POPs.

rachel_network: At this point we can perform edge-orch POP withdraw for ap-pop-5 and ap-pop-12. That will actively cut those POPs out of the fabric and complete the failover. Expect some in-flight requests to reset; drain should finish ~45-75s. Need incident lead signoff.

maya_ops: Notify support and security, then proceed. Jules, please ping impacted customers with ETA. Nate, can you watch for any security anomalies during force withdraw?

jules_support: Notifying CSMs and impacted customers now. Posting a brief status to status.redwood.ai: "Mitigating multi-region failover issue; brief reconnects expected."

security-bot: Automated note: temporary surge in TCP RSTs expected during POP withdraw. Security agents: suppress RST-based alerts for 5m around the change.

nate_sre: I'll monitor. Suppressing RST alerts for the change window and watching auth logs for anomalies.

rachel_network: Executing edge-orch withdraw for ap-pop-5 and ap-pop-12. Capturing tcpdump and fsync of routecache before drop.

```
edge-orch withdraw --pop ap-pop-5 --force --reason "provider-controlplane-delay"
edge-orch withdraw --pop ap-pop-12 --force --reason "provider-controlplane-delay"
# grab traces concurrently
tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/ap-pop-5-pre-withdraw.pcap
```

rachel_network: Withdraw completed. Observability shows eu-central ~99%, ap-southeast health-probes ~1%.

sam_oncall: Post-withdraw telemetry: 5xx returned to baseline (~0.3%), p95 latency normalized. We saw ~1.1k connections reset during cutover (mostly long-poll/streaming), clients retried successfully in most cases.

jules_support: Customer update: most customers reported short reconnects; one high-throughput ingest client saw duplicate chunk uploads due to retry logic. CSMs will contact that account directly. Status page updated with mitigation note.

maya_ops: Root-cause hypothesis: provider control-plane throttled route-withdraw RPCs for ap-southeast-1 causing incomplete withdrawal at two POPs; combined with stale routecache entries at edge fastpath and intermittent LB upstream errors produced partial failover and elevated timeouts. Provider ticket CP-202340 opened.

priya_prod: Uploaded diagnostics bundle and routecache snapshots:

```
s3://rwd-diagnostics/3721119999/diag-bundle.tar.gz
edge-logs: logs/edge-ap-pop-12/3721119999.log
routecache: logs/routecache/ap-pop-5/3721119999.snapshot
```

maya_ops: Incident classification: SEV-2. Mitigations: manual_reweight (canary) then pop_withdraw. Next steps: schedule postmortem, add automation: detect provider withdraw-ack missing > 90s => auto-escalate to POP withdraw or runbook alert; add routecache-check step in runbook to detect pinned fastpath entries; evaluate LB probe jitter and retry backoff to avoid synchronized flapping.

sam_oncall: Handing monitoring/overnight watch to nate_sre. Nate: please watch route-withdraw-ack metric, routecache mismatch count, and 5xx >1% for 5m alert. I'll be offline in 30m.

nate_sre: Taking handoff. Creating suppression for manual-change noise and adding an escalation policy: escalate to oncall if 5xx >1% for 5m. I'll post any regressions here.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigations=[manual_reweight,pop_withdraw], owner=maya_ops, ticket=INC-2026-3721119999

maya_ops: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning owners: rachel_network (network), priya_prod (prod diagnostics), sam_oncall (runbook update). Jules, coordinate customer comms for the postmortem.

jules_support: Will compile customer-impact list and timeline, attach to postmortem. Noted.

security-bot: No anomalous auth or access patterns during withdraw window. Security review not required beyond suppression window.

maya_ops: Closing active mitigation. Monitoring handed to nate_sre. Thank you all.

nate_sre: Acknowledged. Monitoring window started. Will update thread if anything changes.

-- end of thread --
